paper_metadata.title: A 6.3μW 20b Incremental Zoom-ADC with 6ppm INL and 1μV Offset Youngcheol Chae1, Kamran Souri2, Kofi A.A. Makinwa2

figures.label: Fig. 15
figures.caption: Figure 15.5.2 shows a simplified circuit diagram of the ADC. Each integrator is realized with a pseudo-differential inverter-based amplifier. During the sampling phase φ1, the input voltage Vi is sampled on all 64 elements CS, 1-64 (160fF each) of the Cap-DAC. At the same time, the 1st integrator’s amplifier is configured for unity-gain and auto-zeroed with the help of offset-storage capacitor CC. During the integration phase φ2, m elements can be connected to either Vref+ or Vref-,

references.sentence: As shown in Fig. 15.5.1, the proposed zoom ADC combines a coarse SAR conversion with a fine ΔΣ conversion.
As shown in Fig. 15.5.1, the zoom ADC’s output is then obtained by combining the results of the coarse and fine conversions.
Figure 15.5.2 shows a simplified circuit diagram of the ADC.
As shown in Fig. 15.5.3, it consists of a cascoded inverter, which is dynamically biased to enhance its immunity to process, supply, and temperature variations.
The 0.375 mm2 prototype chip (Fig. 15.5.7) is realized in a standard 0.16μm CMOS process.
Fig. 15.5.4 shows the output spectrum of the free-running ΔΣ modulators with DEM on, which is dominated by thermal noise and is free of DEM-related tones.
As shown in Fig. 15.5.5, without DEM its linearity is limited by CapDAC mismatch, resulting in an INL of about 180ppm.
In Fig. 15.5.6, the ADC’s performance is summarized and compared to the state of the art in high-resolution (>14b) incremental ADCs.
